results.summary: This design implements a simple code lock using a state machine. The user enters a code via four input buttons and confirms with an enter button; after three incorrect attempts, the lock disables until reset. The lock output goes low when the correct code is entered. It is intended as a learning exercise and can be tested with buttons and LEDs or a Digilent Analog Discovery.

This project implements an 8-bit pseudo-random number generator using the XorShift32 algorithm. An 8-bit seed is entered via input switches, and after three clock pulses, the first pseudo-random number appears on the bidirectional pins. The seven segment display also shows a random hexadecimal digit based on the current state of the PRNG. It is tested with input switches, a seven segment display, and reading the random outputs at the I/O pins.

This design is a tiny digital synthesizer that accepts a 7-bit MIDI note number and a gate signal to control note on/off. It outputs audio via PWM. The synthesizer generates tones based on the input note. It is intended for audio experimentation and can be connected to a speaker or audio jack.

This design implements a cryptographic accelerator with a cipher core. It uses a SPI interface for configuration and data transfer. The accelerator offloads encryption operations from a host processor. It is suitable for secure communication applications.

This design multiplexes between four VGA projects, with an option to use a true random number generator based on sampling a ring oscillator to randomly select the active project. The multiplexer selects which VGA project is displayed on the output. The random selection is controlled by a TRNG. This allows for a variety of visual outputs.

This design includes a synchronizer, a delay line, and a counter for characterization purposes. It is used to measure delay and synchronization properties. The counter counts events or pulses. This is a test structure for evaluating timing characteristics.

This design wraps a structurally-optimized gate-level multiply-accumulate (MAC) unit in a TinyTapeout-compatible clocked interface. The MAC unit performs multiply-accumulate operations. It is implemented at gate level for optimization. The interface allows integration with TinyTapeout projects.

This design implements a neural network accelerator with fixed-point arithmetic. It includes a multiplier, adder, and register file for computation. The accelerator is designed for machine learning inference. It processes data in a pipelined manner.

This design is a VGA pattern generator that produces test patterns on a VGA display. It uses an oscillator to generate the pixel clock. The output is a video signal with various patterns. It is useful for testing VGA monitors or projects.

This design is notable for its informal and experimental nature. It explores unconventional or playful ideas. The implementation may not follow standard design practices. It serves as a creative exploration in digital design.
